reasons: The rule is a 'missing'-kind check for the presence of a vendor insurance clause; Section 11.6 supplies a usable, mutual insurance regime (workers' comp at statutory limits, employer's liability, general liability with per-occurrence and aggregate limits including clinical trial coverage, A.M. Best-rated insurers, additional insured status, and certificates on request plus claims-made tail), so the compliant classification is supported by the cited text.

No redline or counterparty comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed — consistent with the claimed status and with the deterministic check ('insurance obligation present' = ok).

The absence of an E&O and cyber/privacy layer is correctly treated as a sub-element noted in the rationale rather than a deviation: this is a development/option collaboration in which the counterparty is not hosting or processing Customer Data or working on our premises, so the walk-away trigger (no insurance for a data-processing/on-premises vendor) is not engaged.

Section 11.6.3 (AbbVie self-insurance right) benefits our party, so it is properly not flagged; the rationale appropriately flags the redacted [***] limits for commercial confirmation rather than asserting compliance with specific dollar thresholds.
